purpose: Retained public predecessor and independent current identity transition for an explanatory grammar annotation; no grammar-production or acceptance-rule change.

actql-veca/0.1.admission: These adopted grammar spellings require the VecA scalar node/type/numerical contracts. They are not admitted by the base expression schema or implied by a base text-time implementation claim.

laws.input_evidence_preimages: Input evidence_cid hashes complete canonical JSON: value_contract hashes the checked input contract; literal hashes {version: actql-literal-text-extent/0.1, value: V} for a resolved canonical string, timestamp wire string or known null (zero extent), identically for literal and selected Parameter values; runtime_preflight hashes {version: actql-text-time-runtime-preflight/0.1, contract: C, policy: P} with the complete checked input contract and selected text-time Host policy. Derived outputs use value_contract with the checked child output contract while retaining producer dependencies. Evidence content identity alone never proves applicability to an expression, Program, selected bindings or policy and never discharges demanded child runtime checks. No process-local handle or step index enters these preimages.
laws.consumer_admission: Supplied context contracts are checked even without roots. All known input fields, types and nullability are admitted before predicate demand, including unvisited graph elements. Open contexts do not infer additional field types. Whole-collection and raw-value ceilings are unconditional; evaluated root contract and canonical byte checks are shared with Relation fragments and run once per demanded root before strict-true consumption.
laws.program_binding: actql/0.1 uses this expression contract for every general computation position. The Program semantics envelope includes expression_contract_cid. No source revision inference or compatibility mode exists. Effect selectors retain their closed selector admission.
laws.pure_profile_admission: A live AoA fragment containing any text/time evaluation envelope requires actql-text-time/0.1 with this exact contract CID in required_profiles. A pure_expression descriptor authorizes no acquisition or Artifact barrier. Revalidation derives this requirement from sealed Relation and Graph/temporal consumer fragments, including nonselected branches. Host capability admission is independent of expression demand; a missing profile rejects before execution. Unary try_timestamp is the existing bounded canonical Timestamp conversion, not a patterned text-time evaluation. Its original String conversion retains real scalar work and bounds; admitted Timestamp identity has no invented String/pattern envelope. Explicit value+pattern occurrences keep every existing pattern/profile/envelope obligation. A try_number occurrence whose original checked operand is Number is an ordinary scalar identity, not a String parsing evaluation; it requires no text-time parsing profile or envelope. String occurrences retain the complete profile and envelope requirements.
laws.parameter_binding: General expression parameter references remain in the bound request with their declared checked contracts and copied verified values, not untyped substituted strings or arrays. Invocation and selector values retain their separate binding rules. Bound parameters lower to typed literal roots or typed_null without looking into opaque literal data.
laws.window_aggregate_binding: REL.window.project uses the same expression root positions, filters, folds and aggregate limits as REL.groupBy. Its canonical by parameter contains authored grouping fields only. Group identity, enumeration and output fields prepend window_start and window_end exactly once; these fields must have checked KeyComparable contracts. It never evaluates an argument on a row rejected by that aggregate filter.
laws.null_context_binding: Optional request.null_contexts maps derive step IDs and output names to nullable checked contracts. Each target is exactly a source literal NULL, which lowers to typed_null without changing its source tree. Program checking supplies a context only from independently typed append peers, propagated through field projection/rename and row-preserving steps, or an explicitly mapped nullable ModelTask input. All contributing contracts must have a common join; otherwise checking fails. No arbitrary downstream computation or Effect supplies evidence. Fragment admission validates targets and regenerates typed nodes; Program admission rederives the contextual evidence from Program and admitted contracts.
laws.composition_binding: In an AoA composition, ACTQL.expression_fragment/0.1 has one Relation input and one Relation output; params contains exactly fragment, whose request has the single local source input. ACTQL.predicate_consumer/0.1 params contains exactly consumer and has the signature of consumer.request.operation. Both artifacts are recompiled and compared before composition admission. The canonical composition retains these opcodes and their full sealed material. Sort-checking projections are neither semantic graphs nor executable replacements.
laws.partial_source_evidence: source_schemas records checked field types, including compiler-generated left.name/right.name join provenance. open_sources optionally maps a source to its canonical sorted required column set. Such a source admits additional fields, but no additional type is inferred. Every expression still requires its own type proofs. Pass-through operations preserve openness and unknown columns; derive rejects collision with known or actual input fields. groupBy closes the output field set. output_open is regenerated along with output_schema. Runtime validates all known contracts and required columns and applies value ceilings to all actual fields.
laws.predicate_consumers: actql-predicate-consumer/0.1 self-CID excludes only consumer_cid. The body pins capacity_law and capacity_contract_cid; the registered capacity contract governs whole-input and publication checks independently of predicates, plus demanded context value checks. The request binds operation, closed operation parameters, context schemas and ceilings. Roots are sorted by RFC6901 pointer code-unit order: match_nodes /where uses nodes; match_edges /where uses edges; traverse /hops/i/edge_where and /hops/i/node_where, or homogeneous /edge_where and /node_where, use edges and nodes; sequence /pattern/i/where uses events. Each root is a single REL.where fragment with source input and step condition. Required columns are the sorted context schema keys; no graph property is inferred. Recompile all roots and structural operation constraints before execution. Conditions use the pinned operation traversal/matching demand, never an unconditional prepass over unreachable graph elements. The graph/event carrier and output semantics otherwise remain the pinned AoA laws.
laws.profile_binding: A request containing text-time calls requires text_time_policy, the closed actql-text-time-host-policy/0.1 value. Its canonical CID is host_policy_profile_cid. The fragment evaluations array, including an empty array when no profile calls exist, enumerates every profile call exactly once in expression_pointer code-unit order. node_pointer addresses its lowered node at /roots/index/node; envelope.expression_pointer addresses the source occurrence at /roots/index/source. Envelope semantic_step_id equals the root step_id; demand_path equals the regenerated root demand at that occurrence, including aggregate filters. Admission reconstructs envelopes, bounds, argument identities and both pointers. Literal and checked source extents prove bounds; otherwise expression-local input preflight enforces the selected Host ceiling on demanded evaluations only. Actual successful scalar results satisfy the output ceiling. No callback or provider access is introduced. Unary try_timestamp is the existing bounded canonical Timestamp conversion, not a patterned text-time evaluation. Its original String conversion retains real scalar work and bounds; admitted Timestamp identity has no invented String/pattern envelope. Explicit value+pattern occurrences keep every existing pattern/profile/envelope obligation. A try_number occurrence whose original checked operand is Number is an ordinary scalar identity, not a String parsing evaluation; it requires no text-time parsing profile or envelope. String occurrences retain the complete profile and envelope requirements.
laws.aggregate_binding: REL.groupBy admits count, count_if, sum, avg, min, max, array_agg, string_agg, first, last, percentile_disc, percentile_cont, var_pop, var_samp, stddev_pop and stddev_samp. Authored calls have exactly one field or expr, except row-count count may omit both. Each filter is a separate root and gates demand for that call only. distinct true is admitted only for count with an argument, sum, avg, array_agg and string_agg; explicit false is additionally admitted for row-count count, min and max. Other functions reject the distinct member. Ordered functions use independent total orders, supplied by the analytic frame only in that context. avg requires number; decimal sum uses precision 38 and retains scale. array_agg excludes null and rejects recursively nonconstructible item contracts. Selected first/last values may retain reference and structured contracts. Percentile and statistical laws remain their own deterministic folds; binary64 sum/avg use numeric observation slots. Empty aggregate maps and repeated grouping references are retained; output keys occur once in first-occurrence order, and the empty global group emits one empty row even for empty input. Acceptance never authorizes operation deletion or preimage deduplication.
laws.normalization: Decode without value evaluation. Normalize to_* to cast. Retain typed NULL, identity casts, nesting and array order. Literal payloads are opaque. Predicate is boolean Expression, not a separate value domain.
laws.normalization_fixed_point: Text and structured inputs share alias normalization and closed validation. Whole-field left.id/right.id, including quoted single tokens, normalize to join_field; quoted left/right followed by property access remain ordinary fields. N(N(x))=N(x) and N(print(N(x)))=N(x). Function lookup uses only registered own names. Source intake limits count bytes, tokens, nodes and actual AST depth, including postfix chains; failure is diagnostic, not truncation.
laws.local_type_evidence: Literal NULL accepts the unique domain of its immediate fixed signature, explicit cast or independently typed peer. Overloads without a unique domain do not supply evidence. Independently typed arrays supply item evidence even when max_items is zero; only untyped NULL and untyped [] are excluded. No arbitrary downstream inference.
laws.canonical_omissions: Canonical array nodes are nonempty. Canonical case nodes require else. Empty arrays use checked item contracts and typed_null requires a nullable checked contract. Coalesce remains its dedicated node, never a canonical CASE macro.
laws.demand_derivation: Inherit outer demand. if condition adds none; then adds condition true; else adds condition not_true. CASE condition i adds earlier conditions not_true; branch i additionally adds its condition true; else adds all conditions not_true. Coalesce operand i adds preceding operands null. Aggregate argument adds its own filter true; filter itself adds none. Eager children add none. Admission rederives exact paths from tree and consumer context; tests reuse already evaluated values in the same frame.
laws.representative_failure: Within an expression use prescribed evaluation order. Derive chooses by logical input row order, canonical output field name order, then child evaluation order, never physical completion order. Operation output is atomic, not the entire Run or Effect Set.
laws.evaluation: All branches receive syntax/name/arity/type/profile/static-signature checks. Positional operands are evaluated once in canonical array order; object/derive children in canonical field-name order. AND/OR are eager. if/case demand selected branches; coalesce stops at the first non-null. try_* catches only its own conversion-domain failure, never argument evaluation failure.
laws.boolean: Three values: true,false,null. Conditions select only true; assert_rows requires true. IS TRUE/FALSE/UNKNOWN always returns non-null boolean. DISTINCT FROM uses KeyComparable equality with both-null equal. nullif eagerly evaluates both operands once and returns null only when equality is true.
laws.membership: in and not_in are explicit strict-null propagation exceptions. Evaluate both operands once in canonical order before applying this value rule: a NULL array and an empty array denote the empty set; in is false for every admitted left value on that set, including NULL. On a nonempty set, a NULL left yields NULL; otherwise a matching non-null element yields true even if another element is NULL, then a remaining NULL element yields NULL, otherwise false. not_in is three-valued negation. A NULL array differs from [NULL]. Both return Boolean; max_items zero proves nonnullable, otherwise result nullability is left.nullable OR item.nullable, never array.nullable alone. Scalar domains remain checked. Constant evaluation uses this same rule and preserves failures, demand, logical limits and canonical identity. This law does not admit SQL IN (), UNNEST or subquery syntax.
laws.casts: Closed target table in Language#casts. No implicit conversions. Conversion data is evaluated only on demand. Typed NULL supplies a type; same-type casts preserve their nodes. Decimal conversion from number requires a safe integer; no binary64 fractional approximation.
laws.access: Static closed-object property names; unknown property is a check error, missing declared property an input-contract violation. Subscript evaluates receiver then index; index must be a non-null nonnegative safe-integer number even for null receiver. Valid out-of-range yields null. Reference/json inspection is forbidden.
laws.concat: concat skips null strings, all-null yields empty string. concat_strict and template propagate null. No implicit non-string conversion.

substring.signature: STRING value and safe-integer-valued number start, with an optional safe-integer-valued number length. Result is STRING, nullable exactly when any supplied operand is nullable. Untyped NULL takes the unique positional signature. Retain input max_codepoints and max_utf8_bytes ceilings, but not min_length; do not evaluate length to derive a type. No implicit conversion or BYTES overload is admitted. The number domain is ActQL finite binary64, not the full GoogleSQL INT64 domain.
substring.value: Count Unicode scalars. Positive start is one-based. Zero or a start smaller than negative input scalar length selects the first scalar. Other negative starts count backward from the end, with -1 selecting the last scalar. A start beyond the input returns empty. Omitted length retains the remaining suffix; zero length returns empty; positive length retains at most that many scalars. Negative, fractional or unsafe length, or fractional or unsafe start, fails on a demanded non-null call. Clamp before index addition so safe-integer endpoints cannot overflow. Preserve retained scalars exactly, including NUL, astral, combining and line-break sequences, without normalization.
substring.evaluation: Evaluate value, start and supplied length exactly once in authored order. Apply strict NULL after all supplied children succeed and before index-domain checks. A NULL child never suppresses a later demanded child failure. Preserve enclosing lazy demand, first-failure order, cancellation, workspace, logical work, live-value and output-byte limits. Cooperative scalar counting, boundary location, exact sizing and construction use the existing scalar expression continuation; no Host substring call, secondary evaluator or result remeasurement substitutes for the owner.
substring.identity: The common source is {substring: {value, start, length?}} and the machine node is {op: substring, body: {value, start, length?}}. Preserve omitted length as omitted, distinct from explicit NULL or a supplied length. SQL SUBSTR and SUBSTRING are aliases of this common operation. This current initial-0.1 contract supersedes the inherited fixed-three-argument interval and text-time profile membership for substring. Earlier pinned bodies keep their original meaning and CIDs.
substring.admission: Substring is an ordinary scalar operation, requiring no text-time profile, HostEnvelope or text-time policy. Nested profile operations retain their own profile, pattern, envelope and input-preflight obligations, including in unselected branches. Known input String maxima remain conservative output maxima; otherwise surrounding profile operations retain RuntimePreflight under their selected Host limits. No substring-specific profile extent is invented. Previously derived profile extents across a substring may fall back to this conservative preflight; this ownership migration does not claim identical plan admission for every earlier nested profile expression.

laws.split_part: Preserve empty parts; one-based positive index and negative index from end; zero invalid. Empty delimiter is one whole-string part, including empty input. Out of range is empty string. Null propagates.
laws.lowering: Each normalized expression lowers recursively to a closed actql-expression-node/0.1: op is its canonical tag, body is its normalized payload with expression children lowered. Structural fields and non-null literals are copied, except an immediate Number literal with admitted signed64 comparison context lowers through the exact typed int64 rule. Bound non-null parameters become literal nodes. Every typed NULL, including a null parameter and missing CASE ELSE, becomes typed_null with its nullable checked contract. Explicit casts remain cast nodes around the typed child. Template expands to ordered literal/cast-to-string children under concat_strict, or an empty-string literal for no segments. Empty array becomes empty_array with canonical checked item type. Profile envelopes are sorted by expression pointer. No unselected-expression hoisting or Host callbacks.
laws.envelopes: actql-text-time-bound-laws/0.1 retains pinned Unicode/regex/time bound laws for current profile operations. split_part output ceiling equals input bytes. utf8_truncate uses min(input bytes,max_bytes) for a bound nonnegative safe-integer literal limit, otherwise input bytes. Substring is owned by its scalar law, not a text-time envelope. Bound arithmetic is exact. Parent profile expressions consume child checked extents or retained runtime input preflight. Envelope self-CID excludes only envelope_cid; arguments_cid binds canonical argument subtrees. Demand predicates are outer-to-inner, with earlier branch not_true, selected branch true and coalesce null tests; aggregate arguments begin with their own filter true. No re-evaluation of demand values; no enforcement on undemanded rows; input admission and whole-unit scopes remain enforced.
laws.optimization: Physical optimization preserves canonical identity, demand, first-failure order and logical limits. Failed constant evaluation is not a compilation failure. Physical allocation/CPU usage need not match a reference evaluator.
laws.authority: Effect selectors keep their restricted operand/tree admission. Pure profile evaluation grants no provider access. New node contracts require explicit capability admission; old Plan/contract CIDs retain their prior meaning.
laws.fragment_capacity: actql.expression-fragment.capacity is an extension-local contract-ceiling law. Its source is the canonical bound request CID and exact request pointer; dependencies contain only that CID. Resolved limits retain the existing witness/limit wire shape, engine_atomic enforcement and breach fail. This contract registers the law only for fragment revalidation, not in the shared bound-law registry. Limits are sorted by request pointer and regenerated, including all aggregate max_items guards.
laws.fragment_binding: actql-expression-fragment/0.1 self-CID excludes only fragment_cid. expression_contract_cid pins this contract. request binds source schemas, canonical source pipeline, typed parameter values and ceilings. graph has inline expression nodes at REL.derive /exprs/name, REL.where and REL.assert_all /expr, REL.groupBy /aggs/name/expr and optional /aggs/name/filter. Pointers are relative to params and RFC6901 escaped. Roots are ordered by graph step order then pointer code-unit order; each root stores source, node, checked contract and demand paths rooted at /roots/index/source. Aggregate arguments prepend their own filter-root true test. Admission recompiles request and requires exact equality of graph, root list, types and demand. Schema/self-CID alone is insufficient. Other consumers require a separately admitted binding contract; this revision does not grant them an implicit root position.
laws.ordered_derive_binding: Ordered REL.derive uses the registered row-kernel parameter alternative, with roots at /bindings/i/expr. Bindings remain in authored order; root-list serialization still uses graph-step order then pointer UTF-16 order and does not determine evaluation order. Every field node has exactly one occurrence reference to an input field or earlier slot; literal payloads are opaque. row_kernel_evidence is required exactly when ordered nodes occur, containing their derive bindings and exactly the referenced row contexts and row limits, each once in self-CID order. Regeneration checks complete evidence, same-node/input/type ownership, exact prior-slot prefixes, limits and all self-CIDs. No root or evidence is invented for an absent node. The row-kernel contract is selected through the containing registry, not recursively pinned by this expression contract. Ordered request.pipeline step params contain exactly bindings of name and canonical source expr; parameter references remain source syntax. They contain no references, extension pin, machine nodes or evidence. Graph params contain the selected extension pin, lowered bindings and regenerated references. derive_binding.aoa_node_cid hashes the complete corresponding graph.steps entry {id,in,op,params}, with no wrapper, field omission or evidence. Step and input names are the canonical fragment graph names, not process-local handles.

typed_json_literal.source: A closed typed_literal {type: json, value: decoded JSON text} is an opaque expression leaf. JSON text is data, never expression syntax, a Parameter hole or reference authority.
typed_json_literal.output: The complete JSON value has the existing non-null json contract. JSON null, boolean, number and string are distinct from SQL NULL and ordinary scalar contracts. Existing literal null is SQL NULL; existing ordinary scalar literal inference and object/array literal inference are unchanged.
typed_json_literal.decoding: Decode standard JSON without NFC or newline normalization of data keys or string values. Keep the first occurrence of each exact decoded duplicate object key. Parse and bound the complete input, including discarded duplicates. Preserve array order. Sort object keys by UTF-16 only for canonical encoding.
typed_json_literal.numbers: Use the existing finite binary64 value domain without silent rounding. The original decimal token must roundtrip mathematically through the shortest binary64 decimal spelling; reject precision loss, non-finite values and negative zero explicitly. This is a bounded numeric subset of GoogleSQL JSON, not support for its complete signed/unsigned integer domain. Number token length is at most 1500 characters.
typed_json_literal.bounds: JSON depth is at most 500 and is additionally bounded by the caller depth ceiling. Charge complete decoded source nodes, decoded text and parsing work, including discarded duplicate values. Existing value, expression, canonical-wire and execution ceilings remain applicable. No truncation or partial result is permitted.
typed_json_literal.runtime: The common Value owner retains a JSON domain around an immutable JSON-only payload. Typed runtime recheck rejects a bare scalar or object for a JSON contract; JSON payloads cannot contain typed dates, decimals, vectors or opaque references. IS NULL tests SQL NULL, so JSON null is not SQL NULL.
typed_json_literal.wire: Every non-SQL-NULL JSON cell uses the closed canonical typed-wire envelope {$json: payload}; SQL NULL uses null and requires a nullable contract. Decode this envelope only under a checked JSON contract and an explicit typed-wire entry. An ordinary JSON object with a $json member is payload and is enclosed again; authored raw data never selects a type or authority by its keys.
typed_json_literal.identity: Canonical typed-wire bytes and expression nodes distinguish JSON domains from ordinary scalars and SQL NULL. JSON data keys retain their Unicode scalar sequence. Existing identifier normalization remains separate. Bound wire byte measurements include the envelope. Storage/replay uses the same typed-wire contract and exact pins; old untagged typed JSON wire is not accepted as the new format.
typed_json_literal.consumers: Graph Delta and snapshot identity-body parsers consume an explicitly checked JSON payload through the common read-only accessor. Their semantic body format is not the typed-cell envelope. No graph identity, execution owner or authority is invented by this conversion.

typed_json_wire.representation: Every non-SQL-NULL JSON typed cell is the closed object {$json: payload}. SQL NULL is null and requires a nullable contract. Other typed scalar representations are unchanged.
typed_json_wire.admission: Decode the envelope only in explicit typed-wire admission under a checked JSON contract. Raw authored JSON is not a wire envelope. An object payload containing $json is enclosed again. Reject old untagged JSON cells; no fallback.
typed_json_wire.payload: Retain JSON null, finite canonical numbers, booleans, exact Unicode strings, arrays in order and objects with exact data keys sorted by UTF-16. Typed references and other typed values are not JSON payloads.
typed_json_wire.bounds: Physical wire byte, node and depth accounting includes the envelope. Logical payload accounting counts the JSON payload once. Failure never truncates a value.

abs.signature: Exactly one number operand; the result is number with the operand nullability. Untyped NULL takes the unique number signature. No implicit conversion, decimal overload or non-finite value is admitted.
abs.value: Return the exact binary64 magnitude, including subnormals and the largest finite value. Both zero signs produce canonical positive zero. NULL produces NULL.
abs.evaluation: Evaluate the sole child exactly once when demanded, then apply the value rule. Preserve the child failure, enclosing lazy demand, first-failure order, cancellation and existing logical budgets. ABS introduces no secondary evaluation or value-domain failure for an admitted finite number.
abs.identity: The closed source form is {abs: expression}; the closed machine node is {op: abs, body: expression_node}. Retain the ABS node and its child in canonical lowering. The changed expression contract has its own CID; earlier contract CIDs retain their earlier meaning.

starts_with.signature: Exactly two string operands; the result is boolean and is nullable exactly when either operand is nullable. Untyped NULL takes the unique string signature. No implicit conversion, BYTES overload or explicit collation is admitted.
starts_with.value: Return whether the second string is an exact prefix of the first, using their retained Unicode scalar sequences with default binary comparison. The empty prefix matches every non-null string, including the empty string. A longer prefix does not match. No normalization, case folding, trimming or locale rule is applied. Either NULL operand produces NULL.
starts_with.evaluation: Evaluate the value and then the prefix or suffix once each when demanded, including both children when the first produces NULL. Preserve child failures, enclosing lazy demand, first-failure order, cancellation and existing logical budgets. Exact matching does not skip logical operand charges.
starts_with.identity: The closed source form is {starts_with: [value, prefix]}; the machine node is {op: starts_with, body: [value_node, prefix_node]}. Retain the node and both ordered children in canonical lowering. Earlier expression contract CIDs retain their earlier meaning.

ends_with.signature: Exactly two string operands; the result is boolean and is nullable exactly when either operand is nullable. Untyped NULL takes the unique string signature. No implicit conversion, BYTES overload or explicit collation is admitted.
ends_with.value: Return whether the second string is an exact suffix of the first, using their retained Unicode scalar sequences with default binary comparison. The empty suffix matches every non-null string, including the empty string. A longer suffix does not match. No normalization, case folding, trimming or locale rule is applied. Either NULL operand produces NULL.
ends_with.evaluation: Evaluate the value and then the prefix or suffix once each when demanded, including both children when the first produces NULL. Preserve child failures, enclosing lazy demand, first-failure order, cancellation and existing logical budgets. Exact matching does not skip logical operand charges.
ends_with.identity: The closed source form is {ends_with: [value, suffix]}; the machine node is {op: ends_with, body: [value_node, suffix_node]}. Retain the node and both ordered children in canonical lowering. Earlier expression contract CIDs retain their earlier meaning.

sign.signature: Exactly one finite binary64 number operand; the result is number with the operand nullability. Untyped NULL takes the unique number signature. No implicit conversion, decimal overload or non-finite value is admitted.
sign.value: Return exactly -1 for a negative finite number, canonical positive zero for either zero sign, and exactly 1 for a positive finite number. This includes subnormal and largest finite magnitudes. NULL produces NULL.
sign.evaluation: Evaluate the sole child exactly once when demanded, then apply the value rule. Preserve the child failure, enclosing lazy demand, first-failure order, cancellation and existing logical budgets. SIGN introduces no secondary evaluation or value-domain failure for an admitted finite number.
sign.identity: The closed source form is {sign: expression}; the closed machine node is {op: sign, body: expression_node}. Retain the SIGN node and its child in canonical lowering. Earlier expression contract CIDs retain their earlier meaning.

strpos.signature: Exactly two string operands; the result is a finite number and is nullable exactly when either operand is nullable. Untyped NULL takes the unique string signature. No implicit conversion, BYTES overload or explicit collation is admitted.
strpos.value: Return the 1-based Unicode scalar position of the first exact occurrence of the second string in the first, or canonical positive zero when absent. An empty second string returns 1 for every non-null first string, including the empty string. Count Unicode scalars, not UTF-8 bytes, UTF-16 code units or grapheme clusters. Default binary comparison preserves retained values without normalization, case folding, trimming or locale rules. Either NULL operand produces NULL. Positions are exact integer values in the existing bounded string domain, represented by ActQL finite binary64 number rather than the GoogleSQL INT64 type.
strpos.evaluation: Evaluate the value and then the subvalue once each when demanded, including both children when the first produces NULL. Apply strict NULL only after both evaluations succeed. Preserve child failures, enclosing lazy demand, first-failure order, cancellation and existing logical budgets. Matching preserves logical operand charges; physical search work remains bounded and cancellable.
strpos.identity: The closed source form is {strpos: [value, subvalue]}; the machine node is {op: strpos, body: [value_node, subvalue_node]}. Retain the node and both ordered children in canonical lowering. Earlier expression contract CIDs retain their earlier meaning.

round.signature: One finite binary64 number value operand, or exactly two finite binary64 number operands consisting of value and decimal position N; the result is number and is nullable exactly when any operand is nullable. Untyped NULL takes the unique number signature. N uses ActQL number, not a distinct GoogleSQL INT64 type. No implicit conversion, decimal overload, non-finite value or rounding-mode argument is admitted.
round.value: With one operand, return the nearest integer, rounding exact halfway cases away from zero, preserving already integral numbers including the largest finite magnitudes. With explicit N and non-null operands, require N to be integral; a fractional N fails with the existing arithmetic failure. N > 323 leaves the value unchanged and N < -308 produces canonical positive zero, with both comparisons before any narrowing to a bounded integer. Otherwise use the selected decimal-position algorithm, with negative N selecting positions left of the decimal point and N = 0 retaining the unary value rule. A non-finite ROUND result fails with the existing arithmetic failure. Use the existing ActQL arithmetic canonical positive zero rule. Either NULL operand produces NULL after both child evaluations succeed, before validating the integral N value rule.
round.algorithm: For explicit decimal position select google/googlesql commit 81c15b796138185c046aefe852321011fdf96615, googlesql/common/round_decimal.cc DecimalRounding<false>/RoundDecimal and googlesql/common/double_double.h Full<double>, using the portable non-FMA ComputeDekkerProduct/Split path. Preserve the reference range reductions, exact power-of-five high/low pairs high = RN(5^k), low = RN(5^k - high) for -323 <= k <= 323, FromSum/Fast2Sum correction order, 2^-105 relative-error threshold, sticky-bit adjustment, signed halfway-away selection and Full-by-Full multiply order. RN is binary64 nearest ties-to-even at each prescribed operation. Take the final product high component before the separate final binary power scaling, retaining the additional subnormal rounding. No FMA, reassociation, single binary64 x*10^N calculation or ideal exact-rational decimal rounding may replace this sequence. This pins the selected finite-FLOAT64 algorithm, not live BigQuery behavior or the full INT64/NUMERIC/BIGNUMERIC overload family.
round.evaluation: Evaluate each demanded operand exactly once in authored order, value before explicit N, including the second child after a NULL value. Apply strict NULL only after all demanded child evaluations succeed. Preserve child failures, enclosing lazy demand, first-failure order, cancellation and existing work, frame, workspace and live-value budgets. Decimal-position work remains bounded and cancellable; mathematical no-op cases retain logical operand charges. Unary ROUND introduces no secondary evaluation or value-domain failure for an admitted finite number.
round.identity: The closed source forms are {round: expression} and {round: [value, N]}; the machine node is {op: round, body: expression_node} or {op: round, body: [value_node, N_node]} respectively. Preserve existing unary canonical bytes. Retain the authored ROUND node and every ordered child, including explicit N = 0 and no-op positions; do not fold them into a unary node or constant. Earlier expression contract CIDs retain their earlier meanings and do not acquire the decimal-position overload.

trunc.signature: One finite binary64 number value operand, or exactly two finite binary64 number operands consisting of value and decimal position N; the result is number and is nullable exactly when any operand is nullable. Untyped NULL takes the unique number signature. N uses ActQL number, not a distinct GoogleSQL INT64 type. No implicit conversion, decimal overload, non-finite value or rounding-mode argument is admitted.
trunc.value: With one operand, return the integer obtained by discarding the fractional part toward zero, preserving already integral numbers including the largest finite magnitudes. With explicit N and non-null operands, require N to be integral; a fractional N fails with the existing arithmetic failure. N > 323 leaves the value unchanged and N < -308 produces canonical positive zero, with both comparisons before any narrowing to a bounded integer. Otherwise use the selected decimal-position algorithm, with negative N selecting positions left of the decimal point and N = 0 retaining the unary value rule. Positive position searches forward from that 1-based start; negative position searches backward from scalar length plus position plus one. Count overlapping matches separately. For empty subvalue, match the length-plus-one boundaries: positive position starts at that boundary, while negative position starts at scalar length plus position plus two. Each further occurrence advances one boundary in the search direction; return zero beyond either edge. Empty value and empty subvalue return one at default position/occurrence. Preserve exact strings without normalization.

laws.input_evidence_preimages: Input evidence_cid hashes complete canonical JSON: value_contract hashes the checked input contract; literal hashes {version: actql-literal-text-extent/0.1, value: V} for a resolved canonical string, timestamp wire string or known null (zero extent), identically for literal and selected Parameter values; runtime_preflight hashes {version: actql-text-time-runtime-preflight/0.1, contract: C, policy: P} with the complete checked input contract and selected text-time Host policy. Derived outputs use value_contract with the checked child output contract while retaining producer dependencies. Evidence content identity alone never proves applicability to an expression, Program, selected bindings or policy and never discharges demanded child runtime checks. No process-local handle or step index enters these preimages.
laws.consumer_admission: Supplied context contracts are checked even without roots. All known input fields, types and nullability are admitted before predicate demand, including unvisited graph elements. Open contexts do not infer additional field types. Whole-collection and raw-value ceilings are unconditional; evaluated root contract and canonical byte checks are shared with Relation fragments and run once per demanded root before strict-true consumption.
laws.program_binding: actql/0.1 uses this expression contract for every general computation position. The Program semantics envelope includes expression_contract_cid. No source revision inference or compatibility mode exists. Effect selectors retain their closed selector admission.
laws.pure_profile_admission: A live AoA fragment containing any text/time evaluation envelope requires actql-text-time/0.1 with this exact contract CID in required_profiles. A pure_expression descriptor authorizes no acquisition or Artifact barrier. Revalidation derives this requirement from sealed Relation and Graph/temporal consumer fragments, including nonselected branches. Host capability admission is independent of expression demand; a missing profile rejects before execution. A try_number occurrence whose original checked operand is Number is an ordinary scalar identity, not a String parsing evaluation; it requires no text-time parsing profile or envelope. String occurrences retain the complete profile and envelope requirements.
laws.parameter_binding: General expression parameter references remain in the bound request with their declared checked contracts and copied verified values, not untyped substituted strings or arrays. Invocation and selector values retain their separate binding rules. Bound parameters lower to typed literal roots or typed_null without looking into opaque literal data.
laws.window_aggregate_binding: REL.window.project uses the same expression root positions, filters, folds and aggregate limits as REL.groupBy. Its canonical by parameter contains authored grouping fields only. Group identity, enumeration and output fields prepend window_start and window_end exactly once; these fields must have checked KeyComparable contracts. It never evaluates an argument on a row rejected by that aggregate filter.
laws.null_context_binding: Optional request.null_contexts maps derive step IDs and output names to nullable checked contracts. Each target is exactly a source literal NULL, which lowers to typed_null without changing its source tree. Program checking supplies a context only from independently typed append peers, propagated through field projection/rename and row-preserving steps, or an explicitly mapped nullable ModelTask input. All contributing contracts must have a common join; otherwise checking fails. No arbitrary downstream computation or Effect supplies evidence. Fragment admission validates targets and regenerates typed nodes; Program admission rederives the contextual evidence from Program and admitted contracts.
laws.composition_binding: In an AoA composition, ACTQL.expression_fragment/0.1 has one Relation input and one Relation output; params contains exactly fragment, whose request has the single local source input. ACTQL.predicate_consumer/0.1 params contains exactly consumer and has the signature of consumer.request.operation. Both artifacts are recompiled and compared before composition admission. The canonical composition retains these opcodes and their full sealed material. Sort-checking projections are neither semantic graphs nor executable replacements.
laws.partial_source_evidence: source_schemas records checked field types, including compiler-generated left.name/right.name join provenance. open_sources optionally maps a source to its canonical sorted required column set. Such a source admits additional fields, but no additional type is inferred. Every expression still requires its own type proofs. Pass-through operations preserve openness and unknown columns; derive rejects collision with known or actual input fields. groupBy closes the output field set. output_open is regenerated along with output_schema. Runtime validates all known contracts and required columns and applies value ceilings to all actual fields.
laws.predicate_consumers: actql-predicate-consumer/0.1 self-CID excludes only consumer_cid. The body pins capacity_law and capacity_contract_cid; the registered capacity contract governs whole-input and publication checks independently of predicates, plus demanded context value checks. The request binds operation, closed operation parameters, context schemas and ceilings. Roots are sorted by RFC6901 pointer code-unit order: match_nodes /where uses nodes; match_edges /where uses edges; traverse /hops/i/edge_where and /hops/i/node_where, or homogeneous /edge_where and /node_where, use edges and nodes; sequence /pattern/i/where uses events. Each root is a single REL.where fragment with source input and step condition. Required columns are the sorted context schema keys; no graph property is inferred. Recompile all roots and structural operation constraints before execution. Conditions use the pinned operation traversal/matching demand, never an unconditional prepass over unreachable graph elements. The graph/event carrier and output semantics otherwise remain the pinned AoA laws.
laws.profile_binding: A request containing text-time calls requires text_time_policy, the closed actql-text-time-host-policy/0.1 value. Its canonical CID is host_policy_profile_cid. The fragment evaluations array, including an empty array when no profile calls exist, enumerates every profile call exactly once in expression_pointer code-unit order. node_pointer addresses its lowered node at /roots/index/node; envelope.expression_pointer addresses the source occurrence at /roots/index/source. Envelope semantic_step_id equals the root step_id; demand_path equals the regenerated root demand at that occurrence, including aggregate filters. Admission reconstructs envelopes, bounds, argument identities and both pointers. Literal and checked source extents prove bounds; otherwise expression-local input preflight enforces the selected Host ceiling on demanded evaluations only. Actual successful scalar results satisfy the output ceiling. No callback or provider access is introduced. A try_number occurrence whose original checked operand is Number is an ordinary scalar identity, not a String parsing evaluation; it requires no text-time parsing profile or envelope. String occurrences retain the complete profile and envelope requirements.
laws.aggregate_binding: REL.groupBy admits count, count_if, sum, avg, min, max, array_agg, string_agg, first, last, percentile_disc, percentile_cont, var_pop, var_samp, stddev_pop and stddev_samp. Authored calls have exactly one field or expr, except row-count count may omit both. Each filter is a separate root and gates demand for that call only. distinct true is admitted only for count with an argument, sum, avg, array_agg and string_agg; explicit false is additionally admitted for row-count count, min and max. Other functions reject the distinct member. Ordered functions use independent total orders, supplied by the analytic frame only in that context. avg requires number; decimal sum uses precision 38 and retains scale. array_agg excludes null and rejects recursively nonconstructible item contracts. Selected first/last values may retain reference and structured contracts. Percentile and statistical laws remain their own deterministic folds; binary64 sum/avg use numeric observation slots. Empty aggregate maps and repeated grouping references are retained; output keys occur once in first-occurrence order, and the empty global group emits one empty row even for empty input. Acceptance never authorizes operation deletion or preimage deduplication.
laws.normalization: Decode without value evaluation. Normalize to_* to cast. Retain typed NULL, identity casts, nesting and array order. Literal payloads are opaque. Predicate is boolean Expression, not a separate value domain.
laws.normalization_fixed_point: Text and structured inputs share alias normalization and closed validation. Whole-field left.id/right.id, including quoted single tokens, normalize to join_field; quoted left/right followed by property access remain ordinary fields. N(N(x))=N(x) and N(print(N(x)))=N(x). Function lookup uses only registered own names. Source intake limits count bytes, tokens, nodes and actual AST depth, including postfix chains; failure is diagnostic, not truncation.
laws.local_type_evidence: Literal NULL accepts the unique domain of its immediate fixed signature, explicit cast or independently typed peer. Overloads without a unique domain do not supply evidence. Independently typed arrays supply item evidence even when max_items is zero; only untyped NULL and untyped [] are excluded. No arbitrary downstream inference.
laws.canonical_omissions: Canonical array nodes are nonempty. Canonical case nodes require else. Empty arrays use checked item contracts and typed_null requires a nullable checked contract. Coalesce remains its dedicated node, never a canonical CASE macro.
laws.demand_derivation: Inherit outer demand. if condition adds none; then adds condition true; else adds condition not_true. CASE condition i adds earlier conditions not_true; branch i additionally adds its condition true; else adds all conditions not_true. Coalesce operand i adds preceding operands null. Aggregate argument adds its own filter true; filter itself adds none. Eager children add none. Admission rederives exact paths from tree and consumer context; tests reuse already evaluated values in the same frame.
laws.representative_failure: Within an expression use prescribed evaluation order. Derive chooses by logical input row order, canonical output field name order, then child evaluation order, never physical completion order. Operation output is atomic, not the entire Run or Effect Set.
laws.evaluation: All branches receive syntax/name/arity/type/profile/static-signature checks. Positional operands are evaluated once in canonical array order; object/derive children in canonical field-name order. AND/OR are eager. if/case demand selected branches; coalesce stops at the first non-null. try_* catches only its own conversion-domain failure, never argument evaluation failure.
